characters.name: Echo
characters.description: One of the Los Angeles Dollhouse's most popular dolls. Echo has begun to develop self-awareness independent of her original personality. Action Girl: A frequent imprint, and a defining trait of her integrated personality. Action Survivor: When not imprinted with combat skills she's still dangerous. Be Careful What You Wish For: Caroline wanted to do 'everything'. Well, it happened for her. Blessed with Suck: The emotional isolation of Echo's ability to retain imprints and to be anyone imposed on her, especially how it prevents her from opening her heart fully toPaul Ballard until after he dies in battle. Near the end of his life, Paul tells her, "A hundred personalities, and you're the loneliest person I know."

characters.name: Sierra
characters.description: One of the newest additions to the Dollhouse. Formerly an Australian artist named Priya. The Dollhouse believes they helped her; five years of service in return for curing her severe paranoid schizophrenia.In reality, a high ranking Rossum employee drugged her into psychosis after she rejected his advances, sent her to the House, and rented out her services regularly. She eventually gets her payback. Action Girl: As with Echo, this is a frequent imprint. Amnesiac Lover: No matter what she is imprinted with, she loves Victor. Break the Cutie: Broken before the Dollhouse, and thenagainas a Doll whenshe is repeatedly raped by her original handler. Love at First Sight: When she first meets Victor/Anthony and he is imprinted as an Italian art dealer, she is drawn to him, and almost leaves with him before Nolan intercepts her.

characters.name: Victor
characters.description: One of the most popular male dolls of the Dollhouse. His love for Sierra survives even in his unimprinted state.Formerly Tony, an Iraq war veteran who was recruited after The Dollhouse promised to cure his PTSD. Amnesiac Lover: Is still attracted to Sierra even when in the blank slate mode between engagements when dolls have no sense of self. Love at First Sight: Before Priya/Sierra (Prierra, perhaps?) is a Doll, wealthy Dollhouse customer, Nolan, hires Victor imprinted as an Italian art dealer to lend credibility to an art showing of a piece he commissioned from Priya. His plan backfires, however, when Victor and Priya hit it off. Ooh, Me Accent's Slipping: A notable aversion. Victor is frequently imprinted with personalities of various foreign nationalities just for the sake of giving Enver Gjokaj the chance to show off how good he is at doing different accents. Scars Are Forever: Averted. They'renotablygone by "Vows" (2x01).

characters.name: Adelle De Witt
characters.description: The Dollhouse's 'madam,' in charge of the Los Angeles branch. Outwardly cool, stoic and very British, in her private moments she has revealed a melancholy and loneliness she would die rather than show to her employees. The Alcoholic: Lost total control of her drinking during season 2. Anti-Villain: She is entirely alright with wiping people's minds and sendingmisbehavingDolls or employees to the infamous attic, she also believes she is helping both the Active (a damaged, depressed, down on their luck, etc. person give up five years for care and wealth in the end. Their original personality doesn't even realise any time has passed!) and the client (the often lonely individual gets to fulfill their bizarrest, most secret fantasy). She also truly seems to care for the Actives in her house. Broken Bird: Adelle has nobody in her life that she can truly confess her feelings to, instead using a doll as the closest thing she has to 'company'. The Chessmaster: Easily the biggest one in the show. "I played a bad hand well", indeed.

characters.name: Boyd Langton
characters.description: Echo's gruff but kind handler. An ex-cop, he has serious reservations about the work the Dollhouse does, yet constantly shows unswerving loyalty to Echo. Acts as the moral lodestone of the Dollhouse. Later promoted to head of security. Affably Evil:He's genuinely polite, kind and charming even while manipulating people to his own ends. He genuinely cares about all of the team and considers them "his family". Even when his cover is blown, he never loses his manners. Chekhov's Gunman:The mysterious founder of Rossum Corporation had been hanging out in the LA Dollhouse for two whole seasons, right in front of the viewers faces. Deadpan Snarker: Not as much as Topher, but definitely has his moments - his quips make him come across as theOnly Sane Man.Funny in that he'sfarfrom it - even lampshaded by Topher. Do Unto Others Before They Do Unto Us:He is afraid of imprinting technology bringing about the end of civilization... so he plans on controlling all imprinting technology so that he can cause that apocalypse himself and control the remnants of civilization. Crosses over intoStart X to Stop X.

characters.name: Topher Brink
characters.description: The Los Angeles Dollhouse's genius head programmer. He creates and implants the personalities used by the actives, but has little regard for the morality of what he is doing... at first. Affably Evil: He's actually a very fun person to be around. He just happens to be a sociopath with no morals whatsoever. The Atoner:After realizing he unintentionally caused the Apocalypse. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: He requires a trampoline and a fridge to agree to work for the Dollhouse. Character Development: At first, he only cares about doing thingsFor Science!and doesn't care how his technology is used. As the series goes on, he becomes increasingly disillusioned with Rossum's work and becomes more empathetic, if still rather full of himself.

characters.name: Paul Ballard
characters.description: FBI agent striving to investigate the truth about The Dollhouse, a job described as "the nicest version of fired the bureau has." Like Alpha, he has developed an unhealthy obsession with Echo/Caroline, but you know, a less slashy one. Agent Mulder: In Season One. He is obsessed with finding and exposing the Dollhouse, and his fellow FBI agents, believing the very idea of such a place to be an urban legend, think him a nutjob for it. Badass in a Nice Suit: Wears one both as an FBI agent and as Echo's handler. Boom, Headshot!: How he meets his end in "Epitaph Two: Return": a butcher snipes him when he stops to help Mag. Came Back Wrong: After Alpha renders him braindead by, among other things, physically damaging parts of his brain, Topher and Ivy figure they can reorganize his brain to make him able to function again, but they'll need to overwrite something else to do so. For technical reasons ("The freshest, brightest paths, those are the ones I needed" to quote Topher) they decide to overwrite his emotional connection to Echo that developed over time in "Meet Jane Doe", causing them to undergo aRelationship Reset Button.

characters.name: November
characters.description: November is another female doll in the LA Dollhouse.She spends much of the first season as a sleeper agent, imprinted with the personality of Paul Ballard's lovable neighbour Mellie. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass:She's a "sleeper agent" possessing lethal martial arts abilities when triggered by a code phrase. Curb-Stomp Battle:Against Sierra's first handler, Hearn. Almost literally. Driven to Suicide:She shoots herself in the head when her Mellie imprint comes up against her sleeper imprint, saving Ballard's life. Outliving One's Offspring:She had a daughter who died in unknown circumstances. She joined the Dollhouse to escape her grief.

characters.name: Alpha
characters.description: A former Active, he had 48 personalities downloaded into his brain during a "composite event." He proceeded to get stab-happy and killed his handler, Echo's handler and a dozen other people before escaping. He has an obsession with Echo. He remains a looming presence throughout the first season, and has been known to contact Paul Ballard with information concerning the Dollhouse. A God Am I: Proclaims himself to be one, especially in the Season 1 finale. Alpha constantly mentions how he's above others, and even mentionsblood sacrificesduring one of his rants. Arch-Enemy: To the primarily featured Dollhouse, specifically Echo, Ballard, and Adelle. Ax-Crazy: Even as an innocent doll, he still had the fortitude toslash Whiskey's face repeatedly with bonsai clips and laterpull out all the stops on how to kill people with knives. He even calls his cuts art! Badass Bookworm: Can create and hack into Dollhouse tech with ease.

characters.name: Whiskey
characters.description: One of the most popular dolls before being attacked by Alpha and then implanted with a personality based partially offthe previous (male) Dr. Saunders. The Caretaker: Of the Dollhouse in the future, it seems. Creepy Monotone: In the future. No Name Given: Her original identity is never revealed or addressed in any way. Scars Are Forever: ...or almost.

characters.name: Clyde Randolph
characters.description: The inventor of the imprinting process and co-founder of Rossum.Original RecipeClyde was betrayed by his business partner and became the attic's first occupant-victim. An imprint of him, modified to be unambitious and obedient, now runs things at Rossum. Awesome McCoolname: "Arcane." Lampshaded: "I thought it sounded badass." Dropped a Bridge on Him:He's killed off-screen in the Attic. Fate Worse than Death: What he considers the Attic to be, and let's face it, he's right. Knight Templar: In the Attic, original Clyde is killing people (a) to put them out of their misery, and (b) to help take down the computer mainframe their brains comprise.

characters.name: Clive Ambrose
characters.description: Face of the Rossum Corporation. Body Surf: As of "Epitaph One," he's in at least eleven separate human bodies. Later he joins Harding in constantly jumping from body to body to maintain his power over the ruined world of "Epitaph Two: Return." Even Evil Has Standards: In a way. He disapproves of Harding destroying his 'bodysuits' through excess. Trademark Favorite Food: His original body was allergic to shellfish, so after that's no longer a concern, he develops a real sweet tooth for them.

characters.name: Matthew Harding
characters.description: Adelle's direct superior in the Dollhouse. Big Bad: Even though Clyde andBoydare the true heads of the corporation, Harding is always the more immediate and driving threat throughout the series. Body Surf: As of "Epitaph Two: The Return", he and Clive Ambrose have apparently been switching bodies repeatedly. He even brags to Echo that killing him would just be temporary, since Rossum agents will just upload his personality into another body anyway. Seeing as Topher's device ultimately restored everyone's original personalities, presumably he and Clive are gone for good after that. Cigar Chomper: See the picture. Fat Bastard: In the future.

characters.name: Nolan Kinnard
characters.description: Highly skilled neuro-chemist working for the Rossum Corporation. Knew Priya before she became a doll; when she refused his advances, he drugged her to make her appear psychotic and manipulated the Dollhouse into taking her on as a "humanitarian" case. Defiant to the End: Refuses to apologize or back down, even when his death is imminent. Evil Genius: A brilliant doctor and chemist, but totally amoral, willing to ruin a woman's life just because she bruised his ego. Morally Ambiguous Doctorate: He must not have been paying attention to that "First, do no harm" part of the Hippocratic Oath. Not Good with Rejection: Rejected by a girl you like? Better destroy her entire life, drug her to the point of appearing insane, erase her entire personality and use her as a sex toy to rape and brutalize.

characters.name: Laurence Dominic
characters.description: The Dollhouse's original head of security andDeWitt's number two. He takes his job very seriously but is contemptuous of the dolls themselves. Saves a special dislike for Echo, whose autonomy he considers a security risk.Revealed to beThe Molefor the NSA, wiped and put in The Attic. Deadpan Snarker: 90 percent of his dialogue post Spy In The House of Love counts as this. Hero Antagonist:Dang that pesky lack ofSympathetic P.O.V.. Heel–Face Turn: His motivations don't really change between the first season and the second, but the torture and wet works aspects of his personality are downplayed and he stops trying to kill Echo, making him more of a straight-up heroic character. Imperial Stormtrooper Marksmanship Academy: Shoots eight rounds at his target from point-blank range and doesn't hit her once.

characters.name: Dr. Claire Saunders
characters.description: Chief medical officer at the Dollhouse, she was attacked by Alpha during his composite event and left with bad facial scarring. She is the Dollhouse employee with the most concern for the emotional well-being of the actives.Revealed to be Whiskey, a doll, implanted with a personality based partially off the previous (male) Dr. Saunders, who was killed by Alpha. Broken Bird: As of her discovery thatshe's a former doll. Deadpan Snarker: Half of her dialogue is snark aimed at Topher's expense. Foreshadowing:In 1x08, Caroline demands the release of all the dolls. Guess who's quite casually at the front of the crowd.In another episode, Mr Dominic seems to ask for a strong drink while panicking. Nope, he's just calling "Saunders" under the name he associated her with most. In another episode, Mr Dominic seems to ask for a strong drink while panicking. Nope, he's just calling "Saunders" under the name he associated her with most.

characters.name: Ivy
characters.description: Topher's assistant in the imprint room. She thinks she's here to use her knowledge and technical skills to work the cutting-edge imprinting technology. Topher thinks she is here to bring him snacks. Me's a Crowd: In the comic series, as shown bythis cover. The Igor: Played with in that even though she's Topher's assistant, she's very attractive and far from subservient. Only Sane Man: Easily the most stable programmer we meet. Punch-Clock Villain: To the point where you forget that when she complains about Topher not letting her operate the chair, she's moaning about not being allowed to strip people of their identities and createSex Slaves.

characters.name: Blevins
characters.description: Horrible Judge of Character: He thought Whiskey was a bad influence on Alpha.

characters.name: Sophie Alvarez
characters.description: The Handler: She was in charge of the Active known as Whiskeybefore she was imprinted with the Dr. Saunders personality.

characters.name: Stewart Lipman
characters.description: Groin Attack: Courtesy of Adelle. Jerkass: He's dismissive and condescending to Adelle. Slimeball: He shifts fully into this mode when Adelle briefly flirts with him.

characters.name: Bennett Halverson
characters.description: Topher's counterpart at the Dollhouse located in Washington, D.C. A former friend of Caroline, who was left to die by her in the pastnoteokay, not really; Caroline had Bennett's best interests in mind—it's complicated, which has made her bitter - understandable since Caroline's abandonment left Bennett with a paralyzed left arm. Extremely shy and awkward, and has ahugegeek-crush on Topher. Ax-Crazy: Just a bit. Boom, Headshot!:How she's killed by Saunders. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: She has her ... quirks, but it's obvious everyone puts up with her because of her genius. Cold-Blooded Torture: Subjects Echo to this, as revenge for leaving her to die.

characters.name: Rebecca Mynor
characters.description: A nurse who supported her husband Joel before he became an internet mogul. She did not live long enough to see the house that he would have surprised her with, as she was killed in a car crash on the way, three blocks from the house that Joel wanted her to see. Every year, Joel rents out an Active from the Dollhouse to be Rebecca so that they can have the perfect day they never got to. Hospital Hottie: Was a nurse. Nice Guy: Nice Girl: According to Joel, and from what we saw of her. Ugly Guy, Hot Wife: How Joel described her.

characters.name: Eleanor Penn
characters.description: The second imprinted personality that Echo is shown in and the one that she spends most of the pilot episode in. When the daughter of a prominent businessman is kidnapped, he rents an Active to be a hostage negotiator who can negotiate with the kidnapper for his daughter's return. Prim and Proper Bun: Echo's hair is worn in one while imprinted as Eleanor, with the personality to match. Rape as Backstory: Topher created the imprint of Eleanor Penn by combining traits from several real women, one of whom had been a kidnapping and rape victim as a child. When Echo, as Eleanor, makes eye contact with the kidnapper that she has been hired to negotiate with, she suddenly collapses in paralyzed fear as her mind is flooded with the traumatic memories of that person's ordeal.

characters.name: Jordan
characters.description: The Cast Showoff: Eliza Dushku nails her R&B phrases with beautiful presicion. Ms. Fanservice: She's usually dressed in skimpy outfits, as befitting her role as a back-up dancer for a sexy singer.

characters.name: Roma Klar
characters.description: Honey Trap: For Martin Klar.

characters.name: Anton Lubov
characters.description: The Informant: To Ballard.

characters.name: Taffy
characters.description: Catchphrase: "Blue skies!"

characters.name: Crystal
characters.description: Outlaw Couple: With Bobby.

characters.name: Kiki Turner
characters.description: The Ditz: Calls Chaucer 'Chaucey'.

characters.name: Terry Karrens
characters.description: Living Doll Collector: Uses a drug to paralyze women and use them for his “fantasies.” Serial Killer: The original has murdered countless women, and when Echo is imprinted with his personality she takes up his legacy.

characters.name: Clyde 2. 0
characters.description: An imprinted personality which was created from altering the original personality of Clyde Randolph, one of the co-founders of the Rossum Corporation. Docile in nature, Clyde 2.0 lacked many of the original's traits, thereby working with Boyd Langton without question, being the one to put Clyde Randolph into the Attic. Clyde frequently switched bodies to the point that as of 2007, it was noted that "Clyde Randolph V" was a more appropriate name for him. Big Bad: Well, at least the second or third copy is. The original is locked in the Attic and very bitter. Body Surf: There have been at least five versions of the modified Clyde, plus the original in the Attic. Smug Snake: S(he) is very sure of him/herself, freely taunting Adelle and others. Undying Loyalty: To Boyd, as (s)he is programmed to.

characters.name: Mellie
characters.description: Driven to Suicide: She shoots herself in the head when her Mellie imprint comes up against her sleeper imprint, saving Ballard's life.

characters.name: Bobby
characters.description: Outlaw Couple: with Crystal. Suddenly Shouting: "ARE YOU HAVING FUN, LARS??"

characters.name: Senator Daniel Perrin
characters.description: Happily Married: To Cindy Perrin, or so he thinks.

characters.name: Mag
characters.description: Action Survivor: She was a sociology student at Berkeley before the thought-pocalypse turned her world upside-down. Lipstick Lesbian: More like chapstick.

characters.name: Zone
characters.description: Action Survivor: He was an architect before the thought-pocalypse, and was forced to become this. Fiery Redhead: He is the most choleric, outspoken, and sarcastic character in his group of survivors, who also happens to have red hair. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Shows himself to be this in "Epitaph Two". On one hand, he can't help being sarcastic and anger-prone. But he also has humanizing moments, such as the scene where he calmly admits to Mag that screaming helps him deal with bad news, and his last scene where he seems to accept the now-reset Iris/Caroline as an adoptive daughter. Properly Paranoid: The reason he's still alive. Why Did It Have to Be Snakes?: He seems to exaggerate the justifiable paranoia towards broadcast tech of the others. In the Epitaphs prequel comic we find out why he hates tech so much.It turns out that before the thought-pocalpse hes girlfriend was pregnant with his child and he just found out he was going to be a father... right before she became a mindless tech zombie, meaning he most likely had to kill her.

characters.name: Iris
characters.description: Little Miss Badass: In this case, aJustified Trope: The body is just a vessel with an adult imprint. Older Than They Look: At least mentally.

characters.name: Matt Cargill
characters.description: The Hedonist: He constantly rents out Echo to fulfill his hedonistic desires, particularly on his birthday, which is described as a “three day experiment of pleasure.” Kill It with Fire:Alpha blows him up with a bomb.

characters.name: Gabriel Crestejo
characters.description: Papa Wolf: For his daughter.

characters.name: Richard Connell
characters.description: Hunting the Most Dangerous Game: His plan for Echo. Meaningful Name: He’s named after Richard Connell, the author ofThe Most Dangerous Game, which is fitting, considering he tries to enact the same scenario with Echo.Subverted and invoked, since it turns out it was an alias.

characters.name: Joel Mynor
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: It wouldn’t bePatton Oswaltwithout a healthy dose of snark. The Mourning After: Still grieving for his dead wife. Ugly Guy, Hot Wife: How he viewed himself.

characters.name: Bradley Karrens
characters.description: Bald of Evil: He’s not above using his connections to help hisSerial Killernephew. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He used his connections to make sure his nephew Terry got away with being aSerial Killer. What Happened to the Mouse?: He isn’t seen again after Victor, imprinted with Terry’s personality, causes him to get into a car accident.

characters.name: Graham Tanaka
characters.description: Adoptive Name Change: According toMark Sheppard, he has his stepfather's last name, explaining why there's a white guy called Tanaka. He was originally envisioned as Asian and when Sheppard was cast he asked them not to change the character's name. Jerkass: Enjoys belittling Ballard for his belief in the Dollhouse and generally insulting him. Obstructive Bureaucrat: He takes every opportunity to get in Ballard’s way.
